principle.name: Screenshot Every Distinct Action
principle.description: Capture a screenshot before and after every meaningful user action. A "meaningful action" is any operation that changes page state: click, type, scroll, navigate, form submit, hover-triggered UI change.
principle.rationale: Without screenshots at each step, it is impossible to identify which specific action caused a bug. Post-hoc analysis without per-step screenshots is unreliable.

example.scenario: Debugging a dropdown that fails to show options
example.good: 1. Screenshot before clicking dropdown 2. Click dropdown trigger 3. Wait 500ms for animation 4. Screenshot after click 5. Compare screenshots → options visible? Partially visible? Missing entirely?
example.bad: 1. Click dropdown 2. Wait and assume it worked 3. Single screenshot at end 4. Cannot tell if options appeared and then disappeared

principle.name: Console Capture Always On
principle.description: Register page.on('console') at the start of every debugging session. Also register page.on('pageerror') and page.on('requestfailed').
principle.rationale: Many visual bugs are accompanied by console warnings or errors. Correlating console output with visual state reveals the root cause.

principle.name: Wait for Stability After Actions
principle.description: After any action that triggers async rendering (SPA navigation, animation, API call), wait for network idle or a specific element to be visible before capturing state.
principle.rationale: Capturing mid-transition yields misleading screenshots. Always wait for the target state to settle.

principle.name: Use Locator API, Not XPath
principle.description: Prefer Playwright's locator API (page.getByRole, page.getByText, page.getByTestId, page.locator with CSS selectors) over XPath strings.
principle.rationale: Locator API auto-waits, has better error messages, and is more resilient to DOM changes. XPath is fragile and hard to debug.

principle.name: Isolate the Reproducible Case
principle.description: Before debugging, try to create a minimal reproducible case: clear cookies, use a fresh browser context, disable extensions.
principle.rationale: A clean session eliminates cached state as a variable. The bug should reproduce in a fresh context before investigating further.

principle.name: Prefer Network Interception Over Polling
principle.description: Use page.route() to intercept API calls rather than polling for state changes. This gives you exact request/response data.
principle.rationale: Polling misses transient states. Direct interception provides precise timing and payload visibility.

convention.rule: Use consistent naming pattern for screenshot files
Organize Playwright scripts into logical blocks

pitfall.description: Using headless mode when visual verification is needed
pitfall.why_problematic: Headless mode may render differently (no GPU, different font rendering). Screenshots taken headless may not match real user experience.
pitfall.correct_approach: Use headless: false when debugging visual issues. Use headless: true only for console/network debugging or CI.

pitfall.description: Not waiting for network idle before capturing state
pitfall.why_problematic: Screenshots taken during pending API calls show incomplete page state. Console logs may also be incomplete.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle') or wait for a specific element selector before capturing.

pitfall.why_problematic: After navigation, element references become stale. Trying to read properties from a detached element throws errors.
pitfall.correct_approach: Re-query elements after each navigation using locator API. Use page.evaluate with fresh selectors, not stored references.

pitfall.why_problematic: Console warnings about CORS or mixed content often cause partial rendering failures that appear as visual bugs.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always review ALL console messages, not just errors. Filter and inspect warnings that correlate with the visual issue.

principle.name: Never Equate DOM Visibility with Human Readability
principle.description: An element that passes Playwright's visibility check (offsetParent !== null, getComputedStyle visibility/display) may still be UNREADABLE to humans. Always measure contrast ratio, font size, and opacity — not just presence.
principle.rationale: Text with a 1.36:1 contrast ratio (like rgb(33,37,41) on rgb(45,45,68)) passes every Playwright visibility check but appears as a dark smudge to human eyes. The DOM says "visible" but the human says "can't read it."

example.scenario: Dashboard stats card text is barely readable
example.good: 1. Extract computed text color and background color 2. Compute WCAG contrast ratio → 1.36:1 3. Compare against AA threshold (4.5:1) → FAIL 4. Report: "Text fails WCAG AA by 3.3x — nearly invisible"
example.bad: 1. Check if element is in DOM → yes 2. Check if offsetParent is non-null → yes 3. Report: "Element is visible" → WRONG, human can't read it

principle.name: Always Compute Exact Contrast Ratio, Not Just "Seems Fine"
principle.description: Visual inspection by the model is insufficient for contrast measurement. Always use page.evaluate() to extract exact RGB values and compute the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula.
principle.rationale: Human perception of contrast is unreliable — what looks "slightly dark" to the reviewer may actually be 1.36:1 (3.3x below AA). Only exact RGB extraction + formula computation gives the true answer.

principle.name: Check All Text Sizes for Readability
principle.description: Font size below 12px for body text is often unreadable on standard displays. Font weight below 400 combined with small size is doubly problematic.

checks.check: body text < 12px → WARN "potentially illegible"
fontWeight < 400 AND fontSize < 14px → WARN "light weight too small"
fontWeight < 300 AND fontSize < 16px → FAIL "very light text unreadable"
fontSize < 10px ANY text → FAIL "below minimum readable size"

principle.name: Check Opacity as a Contrast Multiplier
principle.description: Text with reduced opacity (rgba alpha < 1.0, CSS opacity < 1.0) compounds low contrast. A subtitle at 75% opacity with already-low contrast may be effectively invisible.
principle.computation: Effective contrast = raw_contrast_ratio × opacity Example: 1.36 ratio × 0.75 opacity = effectively 1.02:1 — nearly invisible

principle.name: Report Color-Blindness Safety for Status Indicators
principle.description: Status indicators that rely solely on color (red = error, green = success) must also include icons, text, or shape distinctions for color-blind users.

checklist.item: Does the indicator use color + icon/text? → PASS
Does the indicator use color only? → FAIL "not accessible to color-blind users"
Are red/green values distinguishable by luminance? → check luminance delta

principle.name: Check Layout Alignment and Spacing Consistency
principle.description: Visually inspect that all elements align to a consistent grid or layout. Misaligned elements, uneven spacing, and inconsistent padding make a site look unprofessional even if all content is present.

checks.check: Cards/panels have identical padding on all sides → compare computed padding values
Elements in a row share the same vertical baseline → compare margin-top/bottom
No elements overlap or have negative margins unintentionally
Grid columns have consistent gap widths
Headers, body text, and UI elements align to the same left edge

principle.name: Verify Typography Hierarchy is Visually Distinct
principle.description: A proper visual hierarchy uses distinct font sizes, weights, and colors to separate headings from body text. If everything looks the same size, the hierarchy is flat and hard to scan.

checks.check: Heading font size is larger than body text (min 1.25x ratio)
Heading font weight is heavier than body text (min 100 weight difference)
Section headers have spacing above them (margin-top > margin-bottom)
Body text is not the same size as UI labels/buttons

principle.name: Check Border, Shadow, and Visual Treatment Consistency
principle.description: Inconsistent border styles, shadow depths, or corner radii make a UI feel "half-finished." All interactive elements should have consistent visual treatments.

checks.check: All buttons share the same border-radius → FAIL if wildly different
All cards share the same shadow/blur → FAIL if some have shadows and others don't
All clickable elements have hover styles → FAIL if some don't respond to hover
Border colors match the theme — no "forgotten" default borders
Focus indicators exist on all interactive elements

principle.name: Detect Dead Space, Overflow, and Truncation
principle.description: Elements with excessive whitespace, overflow hidden that clips content, or text truncation without indication degrade the visual experience.

checks.check: No text-overflow: ellipsis without a tooltip or expand action
No overflow: hidden that clips content without scroll
No excessive padding/margin that creates large dead zones
No elements with width: 0 or height: 0 that leave gaps
No empty containers that take up space unnecessarily

principle.name: Verify Responsive Layout Doesn't Break at Key Breakpoints
principle.description: A site may look great at 1280px but broken at 375px or 1024px. Test at least 3 viewport widths to catch responsive breakage.

breakpoints.bp: Check nav menu collapse, card layout

checks.check: No horizontal scroll at any breakpoint
No overlapping elements at smaller widths
No elements with overflow hidden that clip at smaller widths
Nav menu collapses correctly at mobile breakpoint
Cards/panels stack vertically at mobile widths

principle.name: Check for "Under Construction" / Unfinished States
principle.description: Placeholder text, lorem ipsum, empty states without helpful messages, broken images, and missing favicons all signal an unfinished site.

checks.check: No "Lorem ipsum" or placeholder text visible
No broken images (img with 0 naturalWidth)
No empty states without helpful messages
favicon.ico exists and loads (not 404)
No "Coming Soon" or "Under Construction" labels for active features

principle.name: Flag Dark Theme Anti-Patterns Automatically
principle.description: Without being told what's wrong, detect common dark design mistakes by extracting all text/background color pairs and comparing against known good dark-mode reference values.
principle.rationale: Many dark themes use pure black backgrounds (#000), pure white text (#fff), or dark text on dark backgrounds — all of which cause eye strain or readability failures. The mode must proactively flag these without the user specifying the problem.

violation.why: Causes eye strain; use #212529, #0a0f12, or #111820 instead
violation.detection: Extract background-color and compare against known-good dark values

violation.pattern: Pure white text (#ffffff) on dark background
violation.detection: Extract text color and compare against known-good dark text values

violation.pattern: Dark/black text on dark background (e.g., #212529 text on #1a1a2e bg)
violation.why: Fails WCAG contrast — text is nearly invisible
violation.detection: Compute WCAG contrast ratio; flag any pair below 4.5:1

violation.pattern: Inverting light mode colors without dark-mode adjustment
violation.why: Dark mode needs specific color rethinking, not simple inversion
violation.detection: Check if dark-mode palette matches Bootstrap 5.3 dark reference values

violation.pattern: Invisible status indicators (dots, badges) on dark backgrounds
violation.why: Status dots with contrast < 3:1 against dark background are invisible
violation.detection: Extract indicator background-color, compute contrast against parent bg

violation.pattern: Low-saturation success/warning colors on dark surfaces
violation.why: Without sufficient luminance boost, semantic colors blend into dark bg
violation.detection: Compare semantic colors against dark-mode reference values

violation.why: Add 2-5% brand hue tint to neutral greys for visual warmth
violation.detection: Check if neutral greys contain any hue component (HSL h !== 0)

violation.pattern: Inconsistent lightness steps in color palette
violation.why: Use systematic scales (10-step, 12-step) for cohesive hierarchy
violation.detection: Extract background lightness values; check if steps are evenly spaced

violation.why: Most interfaces need only primary + danger red + success green + warning orange
violation.detection: Count distinct accent colors used; flag if more than 4-5

principle.name: Status Indicator Design Rules
principle.description: Status indicators (badges, dots, icons) must never rely on color alone. Always pair with shape, symbol, or text label. Test in grayscale to verify color-blind safety.

checks.check: Indicator uses color + icon/text → PASS
Indicator uses color only → FAIL "not accessible to color-blind users"
Indicator contrast ≥ 3:1 against background → PASS
Indicator contrast < 3:1 → FAIL "invisible to users with low-vision"
Indicator distinguishable in grayscale → PASS
Indicator indistinguishable in grayscale → FAIL "relies solely on color"

dark_mode_semantic_colors.color: Dark-mode success green — lighter than light-mode variant
Dark-mode danger red — lighter than light-mode variant
Dark-mode warning orange — lighter than light-mode variant

principle.name: WCAG Contrast Requirement Hierarchy
principle.description: Apply the correct WCAG threshold based on element type, not just a single 4.5:1 rule. Different element types have different requirements.

thresholds.threshold: Text < 18pt or < 14pt bold — WCAG AA requires 4.5:1
Text ≥ 18pt bold or ≥ 22pt regular — WCAG AA requires 3:1
Icons, borders, status indicators — require 3:1 against adjacent colors
Decorative elements with no information — no contrast requirement

principle.name: Color Harmony and Palette Coherence
principle.description: Evaluate whether the page's color palette follows design principles: hue family coherence, brand color adherence, surface hierarchy, and text hierarchy.

checks.check: All colors belong to the same hue family or complementary palette → PASS
Primary/accent colors match brand guidelines → PASS
Accent colors used sparingly (not diluted across too many elements) → PASS
Background surfaces incrementally lighter in dark mode (5-8% lightness steps) → PASS
Body text is off-white, secondary text at ~75% opacity, muted text at ~50% opacity → PASS

principle.name: Bootstrap 5.3 Dark Mode Reference Values
principle.description: Use these reference values as a "known good" baseline when auditing dark-themed interfaces. Flag deviations that reduce readability.

reference_values.value: Standard dark background — not pure black
Standard dark text — off-white, not pure white
Subtle border that remains visible on dark bg

category.name: before_session
category.item: Confirm Playwright is installed and accessible
Set model to qwen3.6-abliterated for vision verification
Identify the exact URL and any credentials needed
Decide browser engine (chromium/firefox/webkit)
Plan the interaction sequence in advance

category.name: during_session
category.item: Register console/error/network listeners before navigation
Screenshot before AND after each action
Wait for stability between captures
Verify authentication state before auth-dependent actions
Record network request/response pairs for API flows
Use locator API with explicit waits

category.name: after_session
category.item: Compile all screenshots into evidence directory
Write evidence.md with structured observations
Compare computed CSS against intended values
Identify root cause or mark inconclusive
Close browser context cleanly

category.name: human_readability_checks
category.item: Extract computed text color and background color for every text element
Compute WCAG contrast ratio — compare against 4.5:1 (AA) and 7:1 (AAA) thresholds
Check font size — flag anything below 12px for body text
Check opacity — flag anything with opacity below 0.75 that also has poor contrast
Check color blindness — flag status indicators that rely solely on color
Generate readability scorecard in evidence.md with element-by-element pass/fail

category.name: visual_polish_checks
category.item: Verify layout alignment — all cards/panels share consistent padding, margin, border-radius
Verify typography hierarchy — heading sizes are distinctly larger than body text
Verify visual treatment consistency — all buttons, cards have matching border/shadow styles
Detect dead space, overflow clipping, or truncated text without indication
Check for unfinished elements — placeholder text, broken images, missing favicon
Generate visual polish scorecard in evidence.md with element-by-element pass/fail

category.name: mobile_verification_checks
category.item: Resize viewport to 375x667 (iPhone SE) — capture full-page screenshot
Test hamburger menu toggle — verify all nav links are accessible
Check for horizontal scroll at mobile width — FAIL if present
Verify cards/panels stack vertically — no overlap, no clipping
Check touch target sizes — all interactive elements are at least 44px tall
Resize viewport to 768x1024 (iPad) — verify tablet layout renders correctly
Return viewport to 1280x720 — confirm no residual layout issues from resize
Capture screenshots at each breakpoint for evidence
